summary: ArgonautX: cascading fallback amplification causing duplicate completions, billing spike, and streaming disconnects — post-incident follow-up
description:
Issue summary:
ArgonautX reported elevated token billing, duplicate completions, and intermittent streaming disconnects for a subset of chat API calls beginning ~2026-02-20T02:12:00Z. The problem coincided with a peak of concurrent requests from ArgonautX and a control-plane routing jitter where primary model allocations briefly failed and multiple fallback routes were attempted in rapid succession.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: intermittent truncated streams for ~12% of requests during the window (02:12–02:55 UTC).
- Billing: preliminary estimate shows a ~3.6x token billing amplification for affected sessions due to duplicate/completed retries.
- Availability: overall API success rate for ArgonautX dropped from 99.98% to 97.3% for the 40-minute window.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod/us-east), customer on enterprise plan with pinned model policy to starling-v1 with fallback to starling-v1-quantized.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Replayed a portion of ArgonautX traffic against prod-like cluster with concurrency burst tools.
2) Triggered a simulated allocation timeout on primary route to observe fallback behavior.
3) Observed multiple overlapping fallback executions per request, streaming connection resets, and duplicate transcript completions.

Logs / Observed traces:
- Control plane logs show repeated routing attempts (router: route_attempt=3..7) for identical request IDs within ~600ms windows.
- Serving runtime traces show KV cache warmup restarted for each fallback attempt resulting in repeated token generation for the same client session.
- Billing telemetry flagged high token counts tied to the same session_id hash.

Action requested by customer:
- Detailed breakdown of token billing per request/session during the incident window, and credits for duplicated token usage where amplification is confirmed.

Desired outcome:
- Customer wants the billing delta reversed for duplicated/completed requests, details on root cause, and a mitigation plan so this doesn't recur.
comments: 2026-02-20 02:24 UTC — Priya Nair (Support): Acknowledged receipt from ArgonautX. Opening Major Incident ticket and engaging SRE. Requested exact timeframe and sample request IDs. SLA P0 initiated.

2026-02-20 02:37 UTC — ArgonautX (Customer): Provided three sample request IDs and mentioned a 5x increase in token consumption on their invoicing dashboard. Said streaming clients saw truncated messages and duplicate final tokens twice in the transcript.

2026-02-20 02:45 UTC — Jared Ortiz (SRE): Initial triage indicates routing jitter in the us-east control plane region. We observed route fallback storms when allocation acknowledgements timed out. Hotfix: added a guard to limit parallel fallback attempts to 1 per request_id. Deploying to canary in 2 AZs.

2026-02-20 03:05 UTC — Support: Customer notified of temporary mitigation (fallback parallelism cap) and asked to monitor. Also recommended immediate pin to primary model to avoid quantized fallback until further analysis.

2026-02-20 04:10 UTC — ArgonautX: Confirmed visible improvement after mitigation; streaming truncation rate dropped and token counts normalized for new requests. Asked for a retroactive billing reconciliation and a permanent fix timeline.

2026-02-26 16:45 UTC — Jared Ortiz: Permanent fix merged (PR #2345) — router now serializes fallback attempts, de-duplicates in-flight fallback executions, and adds a short idempotency token to the request path to prevent duplicate completions. Notified billing to compute credits for confirmed duplicates.

2026-02-26 17:10 UTC — Priya Nair: Closed loop with ArgonautX. Customer accepted mitigation and requested invoice adjustment; billing team to issue credit for amplified tokens. Customer asked for a short writeup for their security/compliance team explaining the change — link provided to Confluence page.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Allocation ack timeouts at control-plane level caused router to retry routing decisions aggressively, spawning multiple fallbacks for the same logical request.
Telemetry: Correlation between router retry spikes and KV-cache warmup reinitializations in the serving runtime. Trace IDs show identical session_id producing multiple final_token events within 1s.
Root cause: Race in routing ack handling — ack lost during control-plane GC cycle under high connection churn; router lacked a global request-level in-flight dedupe prior to fallback execution.
Scope: Effect primarily for customers with pinned model + quantized fallback policy when concurrency > ~1200 RPS in us-east. Not a model-quality issue; it's an orchestration/routing failure mode.
Counterfactual checks: No evidence of model duplication in serving logs outside of fallback windows; this confirms duplication stems from repeated fallback invocations rather than downstream replay.
Risk assessment: High customer impact and billing exposure; low probability for customers not using fallback chains. Mitigation recommended across regions.
Monitoring additions: Added dashboard panels to surface routing_attempts_per_request and duplicate_final_tokens_by_session_id; alerting at >0.1% duplicate rate per customer for 5m.
Temporary mitigation validation: Canary with fallback cap reduced duplicate rate from 3.6% to 0.05% for ArgonautX traffic replay.
resolution: Workaround applied (2026-02-20): limited parallel fallback attempts per request to 1 and recommended customer pin to primary model to avoid quantized fallback. Permanent fix (deployed 2026-02-26): router serialized fallback execution, added request-level in-flight deduplication, and introduced a short idempotency token to serving path to prevent duplicate completions. Billing: Eng has provided timestamped list of duplicated request IDs to Billing; Billing to issue credit for duplicated tokens in ArgonautX's Feb invoice. Follow-ups: (1) Production rollout verification in eu-west and ap-southeast by 2026-03-03, (2) postmortem writeup published, (3) SRE-run tabletop with Support & Billing to update runbooks and billing reconciliation playbook.
